open_points.subject: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner — deterministic backend IR values
open_points.text: A value of a deterministic backend's IR is held only by the module emitted from it and by no constant: the media types, signatures and download names of `binary_storage` (`rules.binary_delivery_policy`), the table names of the repositories, the hashing parameters of `credential_security`.
open_points.question: Is the authoritative owner of each value its backend IR, which necessarily records the value, or the emitted module that this sentence says holds it exclusively?
options: The backend IR is the design-time owner and the emitted module only contains its generated runtime representation.
The emitted module owns the value; the IR merely generates it and is not an authoritative record.
Both the IR and emitted module own the value, despite the statement that only the module holds it.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the backend IR as the sole design-time authority and the emitted module as a generated runtime representation, and rewrite “held only” to distinguish those roles.

witness.initial: `rules.binary_delivery_policy` records one media signature and `binary_storage` has been emitted from it.
events: A specification author changes the signature in `rules.binary_delivery_policy`.
A maintainer decides whether the IR change is authoritative immediately or whether the emitted `binary_storage` module remains the owner until regeneration.
outcomes: The IR is authoritative, so the next generation uses the changed signature and direct edits to the module are invalid.
The emitted module is authoritative, so changing only the IR does not change the owned value and may later conflict with the module.
witness.observer: A client whose binary matches only one of the two signatures sees acceptance in one implementation and `BinaryStorageError` in the other.

open_points.subject: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner — repository table names
open_points.text: A value of a deterministic backend's IR is held only by the module emitted from it and by no constant: the media types, signatures and download names of `binary_storage` (`rules.binary_delivery_policy`), the table names of the repositories, the hashing parameters of `credential_security`.
open_points.question: How can repository table names be held only by emitted repository modules when the same unit also says “Table names are `config.persistence` (A30)” and earlier text says the persistence closure carries them; which record or module is their one owner?
options: `config.persistence`/the persistence backend IR owns all table names, and each emitted repository receives the names it uses.
Each repository module owns its own table names, while `config.persistence` is only non-authoritative generator input.
A shared emitted persistence module owns the table names and repositories import them from it.
open_points.default_guess: Make the persistence backend IR sourced from `config.persistence` the authority and emit each name into every repository or bootstrap adapter that needs it without creating a second design-time owner.

witness.initial: An empty deployment has staff and audit tables used by the bootstrap path and later by ordinary repository-backed operations.
events: The host operator runs `staff_bootstrap_store`, which inserts the first staff account and its audit record.
The service later authenticates that account through the normal repositories.
Implementers independently choose whether bootstrap and normal repositories share names from the persistence IR or each module owns its own literal names.
outcomes: Both paths use names emitted from one persistence definition, so the account and audit record are found.
The modules independently own their table-name values; a differing generated or migrated name lets bootstrap succeed but leaves the normal repository unable to find the records.
witness.observer: The host operator and first administrator see whether the newly bootstrapped account can log in.

open_points.subject: Facts several modules touch, and their one owner — scope of the deterministic-backend exception
open_points.text: A value of a deterministic backend's IR is held only by the module emitted from it and by no constant: the media types, signatures and download names of `binary_storage` (`rules.binary_delivery_policy`), the table names of the repositories, the hashing parameters of `credential_security`.
open_points.question: Is the list after the colon exhaustive, or does every fixed value in any deterministic backend IR—including values such as viewer-cookie attributes—belong only to its emitted module and never to `data_provider`?
options: The three listed groups are the complete exceptions.
They are examples; every deterministic-backend IR value is excluded from `data_provider`.
Only values exclusively consumed by an emitted backend are excluded; a value also read by model-written code must instead be a `data_provider` constant.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the list as examples and apply the exception to values consumed exclusively by a deterministic emitted backend; explicitly decide mixed-consumer values.

witness.initial: The viewer cookie name and attributes are fixed release policy values read by the deterministic viewer-cookie backend, while the new sentence names only binary, repository and credential-security values.
events: One implementer reads the colon list as exhaustive and places the cookie values according to the preceding `data_provider` rule.
Another reads the sentence as a general deterministic-backend rule and leaves the cookie values only in the viewer-cookie backend IR.
outcomes: `api_irregular` imports cookie policy through a `data_provider` constant and gains that dependency.
`api_irregular` is emitted with the cookie policy from its backend IR and has no `data_provider` dependency for it.
witness.observer: The spec projector and dependency-graph reviewer see different import surfaces and affected sets.
